decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom was a heavy, visibly announced investment central to the firm's radiotherapy QA direction, and its slow uptake can still be blamed on regulatory release timing and the small particle therapy market, so management persists.
Small volume chambers are a core part of the dosimetry portfolio, carry sunk calibration and certification investment, and showed stable dedicated presentation.
This chamber fits the firm's announced small-field dosimetry line, has had steady visibility since launch, and is cheap to keep alongside the sunk development costs.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple product with ongoing demand and recalibration revenue, so dropping it would contradict the firm's core commitment.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantom systems, and its continued own page signals ongoing commitment.
Thimble chambers are a long-lived standard product in the line, with low running costs and invested certification, so the firm keeps it.
